scholarships.title: Danish Government Scholarship for Non-EU/EEA Full-Degree Students
scholarships.official_source: Danish Ministry of Science, Higher Education and Digital Affairs (Study in Denmark)

existing.description: Danish universities receive a limited number of government scholarships each year to fund highly qualified full-degree students from countries outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland. Applicants must be citizens of a non-EU/EEA/non-Swiss country, enrolled in a full degree programme and hold a time-limited residence permit for education, and they are excluded if they seek admission to an artistic higher education institution, have a legal claim to Danish citizens' rights, or are eligible for SU. The scholarship consists of two parts and may be a full or partial tuition fee waiver, a grant towards living costs, or both. The individual university administers the award and selects the students.
eligibility: A citizen of a country outside the EU, the European Economic Area or Switzerland
Enrolled in a full degree higher education programme
Granted a time-limited residence permit in Denmark due to education
Not applying to an Artistic Higher Education Institution
No legal claim to the rights of Danish citizens
Not eligible for a grant under Danish State Education Fund (SU) rules
Not holding a residence permit under Aliens Consolidations Act section 9c(1) as a child of a section 9m permit holder who is a non-EU/EEA national
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens of countries outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland who are enrolled, or applying, in a full degree higher education programme in Denmark and hold a time-limited residence permit granted for education.
benefits: Full or partial tuition fee waiver as decided by the university
Some universities also award a grant towards living costs
The ministry states the scholarship 'consists of two parts'
coverage: Full or partial tuition fee waiver
Depends entirely on the administering university
documents: Documents required by the admission application of the chosen university
existing.english_requirement: taught study programme. There should be one to fit your academic aspirations.
application_method: Apply through the admission process of the individual Danish higher education institution, which selects and awards the scholarship holders
existing.selection_notes: The scholarship is highly competitive because the ministry states universities receive only a limited number each year; selection is entirely in the hands of each university.
existing.best_fit: Highly qualified non-EU/EEA students admitted to Danish universities
existing.notes: The ministry page explicitly warns that because the scholarships are administered by the institutions themselves, applicants should enquire directly at their chosen institution for the current terms. Separate schemes listed on the same page include Nordplus, Erasmus, Erasmus Mundus, Fulbright Denmark and the Danish State Educational Support (SU), which is generally only for Danish residents.
existing.deadline_display: The ministry publishes no deadline: 'The scholarships are administered by the Danish universities, who each select the students, who are awarded with a scholarship. For further information about the government scholarship, please consult the admission details of the higher education institution of your choice.' The deadline is therefore the admission deadline of the individual university.
existing.program_type: Government-funded tuition waiver administered by universities
